entries.knownHazards: Bermuda grass is reported to be photosensitizing in animals[269]. Under certain environmental conditions the plant can produce hydrocyanic acid and so is potentially toxic to livestock[274]. The plant is also said to cause contact dermatitis and, with its high production of pollen, can be a major cause of hayfever[269, 274].

entries.knownHazards: The seeds, and the oil, contain cyclopropenoid fatty acids such as malvalic acid (7 - 8%) and sterculic acid (3%), which cause abnormal physiological reactions in animals. Therefore the consumption of kapok seeds or seed oil should be discouraged unless the cyclopropenoid acids have been chemically removed[ 299 ]. Kapok fibre is irritating to the eyes, nose and throat, and workers exposed to kapok dust for long periods may develop chronic bronchitis[ 299 ]. (Plant has spines or sharp edges; use extreme caution when handling )
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Sėklose ir aliejuje yra ciklopropeno riebalų rūgščių (malvalio ir sterkulo rūgštys), kurios sukelia patologines reakcijas gyvūnams — nevartoti be cheminio valymo. Kapokinės skaidulos dirgina akis, nosį ir gerklę; ilgalaikis dulkių poveikis gali sukelti lėtinį bronchitą. Augalas turi spyglius — elgtis atsargiai.

entries.knownHazards: The plant is reported to contain a toxic saponin[274]. Although toxic, saponins are poorly absorbed by the body and most pass straight through without any problem. They are also broken down to a large extent in the cooking process. Saponins are found in many foods, such as some beans. Saponins are much more toxic to some creatures, such as fish, and hunting tribes have traditionally put large quantities of them in streams, lakes etc in order to stupefy or kill the fish[K].

entries.knownHazards: Like many other plants in the Fabaceae family, Chamaecytisus species can contain alkaloids (notably cytisine), which are toxic when ingested in significant quantities. Cytisine can cause Nausea and vomiting, Abdominal pain, and Respiratory issues in severe cases. Pets, livestock, and humans (especially children) should avoid consuming parts of the plant. Allergenic Potential: Some individuals may develop skin irritation or allergic reactions when handling the plant, particularly during flowering or seed pod development.
